Document type: adjuster_file. Page 1 of 2.

<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1180
Claimant:
James Smith
Adjuster:
Christopher Wong
1-3-25
First notice of loss received for a rear-end collision at a low-speed intersection. The insured's vehicle was struck from
behind while stopped, and the claimant reports a knee injury. The claimant is represented by counsel, so all further
contact will go through the attorney's office.
1-29-25
Confirmed that the driver of the vehicle involved is named on the policy and that coverage was in force on the date of
loss. Opened bodily injury and property damage feature files.
3-25-25
Spoke with the other driver, who confirmed the accident happened as the claimant described it. The other driver's
account matches the claimant's in every detail that was discussed.
4-8-25
Police report obtained. It lists the claimant as a passenger in the vehicle at the time of impact, consistent with
statements from both the claimant and witnesses.
4-25-25
Reviewed scene photographs and a statement from an independent witness. Both support the account of how the
collision occurred. Vehicle damage appears largely consistent with the described impact.
4-28-25
Obtained the vehicle's prior repair history. No earlier damgae to the vehicle is on record, and nothing in the file
suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.
5-10-25
Claimant's attorney submitted the initial medical records. The reported knee injury is a plausible result of a collision of
this type.
5-15-25
Reviewed the claimant's medical history with the attorney's office. No prior injury to the same body area is known,
and the claimant has told the same account of the accident in every conversation so far.
5-26-25
Treatment began with a standard course of physical therapy and imaging. Records show the care followed a typical
progression for this type of injury.
5-31-25
Medical updates indicate steady improvement. Therapy visits have been reducing in frequency as the claimant's
condition gets better.
6-18-25
Received follow-up records showing treatment has tapered off as expected. The claimant has not reported any new
symptoms or additional providers.
6-30-25
Reviewed the full file with the supervisor. The claim appears consistent throughout, and the injury and damage align
with the reported accident. Next step is to finalize the medical evaluation with the attorney's office.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
